program.name: Child and Dependent Care Credit (CDCC)
program.description_short: Federal tax credit for child or dependent care costs while you work or look for work
program.description:
This federal tax credit helps pay for care for your child under 13, or for your spouse or another adult who can’t take care of themselves, so you can work or look for work. It lowers the federal income tax you owe, but only down to zero. If you don’t owe any federal income tax, it won’t give you money back.

You get the credit once a year when you file your federal taxes. The amount shown is an estimate based on your income and care costs. There are some things we couldn’t check, so please read the following to make sure you qualify.

Your child must have lived with you for more than half the year. If you’re divorced or separated, only the parent the child lived with most of the year can get the credit. An adult, including your spouse, counts only if they lived with you more than half the year and can’t do basic things on their own, like getting dressed, bathing, or eating.

The credit is based on what you pay for care, but only some care counts. Daycare, a babysitter or nanny, preschool, before- and after-school care, and day camp count. School costs for kindergarten and up, and overnight camp, don’t. Leave out costs that don’t count when you add up your care costs, or your credit will be lower than you expect. Money you pay to your spouse, your child’s other parent, anyone you claim as a dependent, or your own child under 19 also doesn’t count.

If you’re married, you usually need to file taxes together with your spouse, which is called a “joint return.” If you got combat pay that isn’t taxed, you can choose to count it as work income. If you’re self-employed and lost money, that loss lowers your work income and can change your credit.

Taxes are due April 15 for most people. Refunds usually arrive about 3 weeks after you file online, or 6 or more weeks if you file by mail.

To claim this credit, select File Taxes to learn how to fill out Form 2441 and send it with your tax return.

navigators.name: VITA Free Tax Preparation (IRS Volunteer Income Tax Assistance)
navigators.description: Free tax help from trained IRS volunteers for people with low to moderate income, people with disabilities, and people who speak limited English. They can help you file your federal return and claim the Child and Dependent Care Credit.

navigators.name: AARP Foundation Tax-Aide
navigators.description: Free tax help from IRS-certified volunteers, with a special focus on people over 50 with low to moderate income. Volunteers can help you claim the Child and Dependent Care Credit on your federal return. The site locator is open January through April.
